clues: I was formed from the dust of the ground, and God breathed life into my nostrils.
I was told to name every living creature, and I gave my wife the name Eve.
I was the first man, and I ate the fruit my wife handed me in the garden of Eden.
I was made from a rib while the first man slept.
A serpent told me I would not surely die, and I believed him.
I am called the mother of all living, and my name means life.
I found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the whole earth was corrupt.
I built something enormous out of gopher wood, exactly as I was told.
I gathered animals two by two before the flood, and later saw a rainbow.
God changed my name and promised my descendants would outnumber the stars.
I left Ur and Haran for a land I had never seen, at seventy-five years old.
I am called the father of faith, and I was ready to offer up my son Isaac.
I laughed when I overheard a promise about my own body.
I gave my maid Hagar to my husband, and later regretted it.
I bore Isaac at ninety years old, and my husband was Abraham.
My name means laughter, because of how my mother received the news of me.
I carried the wood for my own sacrifice up a mountain, but a ram took my place.
I was the son of Abraham and Sarah, and the father of Jacob and Esau.
I was born gripping my brother's heel, and I lived up to that start.
I wrestled until daybreak and walked away with a limp and a new name.
I had twelve sons, and I loved Joseph most of all.
My brothers hated me for my dreams and sold me for twenty pieces of silver.
I interpreted dreams in a prison, then interpreted one for Pharaoh himself.
I wore a coat of many colors and became ruler over all Egypt.
I was hidden in a basket among the reeds of a river.
I argued that I was slow of speech, so my brother spoke for me.
I parted the Red Sea and received the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai.
My rod swallowed the rods of Pharaoh's magicians after it became a serpent.
I made a golden calf while my brother was up on the mountain.
I was the first high priest of Israel, and Moses was my brother.
I watched a basket float in the Nile and spoke up to a princess.
I was struck with leprosy for seven days after speaking against my brother.
I took a timbrel and led the women in song after the Red Sea, and Moses was my brother.
I was one of only two spies who came back with a good report.
I was told to be strong and of good courage, for the Lord would be with me.
I marched around Jericho for seven days until its walls fell flat.
I said we are well able to overcome them, when ten others said otherwise.
At eighty-five I claimed I was as strong as I was at forty.
I was the other faithful spy alongside Joshua, and I asked for Hebron.
I hid two strangers under stalks of flax on my roof.
I tied a scarlet cord in my window so my household would be spared.
I was a harlot of Jericho, and I am listed in the genealogy of Christ.
I asked for a sign twice using a fleece and the morning dew.
My army was cut from thirty-two thousand down to three hundred.
I defeated the Midianites with trumpets, pitchers, and lamps.
I killed a lion with my bare hands and later found honey in its carcass.
I slew a thousand men with the jawbone of a donkey.
My strength was in my hair, and Delilah betrayed me to the Philistines.
I judged Israel while sitting under a palm tree.
I told a commander I would go with him, since he would not go alone.
I was a prophetess and judge, and I sang a song of victory with Barak.
I was a Moabite widow who refused to return to my own people.
I said where you go I will go, and your God will be my God.
I gleaned in the fields of Boaz and became great-grandmother to King David.
I lost my husband and both of my sons in a foreign land.
I told the women to call me Bitter instead of Pleasant.
I was Ruth's mother-in-law, and I told her to lie at the feet of Boaz.
My mother lent me to the Lord before I was born.
I heard a voice at night three times and thought it was the priest Eli.
I anointed both Saul and David as king over Israel.
I wept and would not eat, because the Lord had shut up my womb.
A priest thought I was drunk, but I was only pouring out my soul.
I vowed my son to the Lord, and I was the mother of Samuel.
I was head and shoulders taller than any of my people.
I was out looking for lost donkeys when I was told I would be king.
I was Israel's first king, and I consulted a witch at Endor before I died.
I was the youngest of eight sons, and I kept my father's sheep.
I played the harp to soothe a troubled king, and I wrote many psalms.
I killed Goliath with a sling and a stone, and later became king of Israel.
I was six cubits and a span tall, and my coat of mail weighed five thousand shekels.
I defied the armies of Israel for forty days and no one would answer me.
I was the champion of Gath, and a shepherd boy felled me with one stone.
I climbed a cliff with my armorbearer and routed a Philistine garrison.
I ate honey in a wood, not knowing my father had cursed anyone who ate.
My soul was knit to David's, and my father was King Saul.
God offered me anything, and I asked for an understanding heart.
I settled a dispute between two women by calling for a sword.
I built the temple in Jerusalem, and the Queen of Sheba came to test me.
Ravens brought me bread and flesh by a brook called Cherith.
I called down fire on a soaked altar and mocked the prophets of Baal.
I went up to heaven in a whirlwind with a chariot of fire, and Elisha watched.
I was plowing with twelve oxen when a mantle was thrown over me.
I asked for a double portion of my master's spirit.
I made an axe head float and told Naaman to dip seven times in the Jordan.
I was a mighty man of valor, but I was a leper.
A little captive maid told my wife where I could be healed.
I was angry at being told to wash in the Jordan, but I dipped seven times and was clean.
I was a king's wife from Sidon, and I fed hundreds of false prophets.
I wrote letters in my husband's name to seize a man's vineyard.
I painted my face and looked out a window before being thrown down to the dogs.
I spread a threatening letter before the Lord in the temple.
I was told to set my house in order, so I turned to the wall and wept.
Fifteen years were added to my life, and the sun's shadow went backward ten degrees.
I became king when I was only eight years old.
I tore my clothes when the book of the law was read to me.
I destroyed the idols and kept the greatest Passover since the days of Samuel.
I was a cupbearer to a Persian king, and my face was sad before him.
I inspected broken walls by night, riding alone.
I rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem in fifty-two days while my workers held weapons.
I was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses.
I proclaimed a fast at the river Ahava rather than ask the king for soldiers.
I read the law aloud from morning until midday while the people wept.
I was an orphan raised by my cousin, and I hid my nationality.
I was told that I had come to the kingdom for such a time as this.
I went in to the king unbidden and saved my people from Haman.
I refused to bow, and a powerful man plotted genocide over it.
I sat in sackcloth at the king's gate and sent word to my cousin.
I was Esther's cousin, and I rode through the city in royal apparel.
I was perfect and upright, and I feared God and shunned evil.
I lost my children, my wealth, and my health in a single season.
I said though he slay me, yet will I trust him, and my three friends accused me.
I refused the king's meat and wine, asking for pulse and water instead.
I read the writing on the wall when no one else could.
I prayed three times a day and spent a night in a den of lions.
I paid my fare and boarded a ship going the opposite way.
I slept through a storm until the sailors cast lots and found me out.
I spent three days in a great fish, then preached to Nineveh.
I saw the Lord high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
I cried woe is me, for I am a man of unclean lips, and a coal touched my mouth.
I said here am I, send me, and I foretold a virgin would bear a son.
I said I am a child and cannot speak, but God had known me before I was formed.
I was lowered into a dungeon of mire and sank in the mud.
I am called the weeping prophet, and I wrote Lamentations over Jerusalem.
I saw a whirlwind out of the north and living creatures with four faces.
I was told to eat a scroll, and it was sweet as honey in my mouth.
I prophesied to a valley of dry bones until they lived and stood up.
My father was struck dumb until the day I was named.
I wore camel's hair and a leather girdle, and I ate locusts and wild honey.
I baptized in the Jordan and said he must increase but I must decrease.
An angel greeted me as highly favored and told me not to fear.
I asked how this could be, and I was told nothing is impossible with God.
I laid my firstborn in a manger, and I stood near the cross when he died.
I left my nets to follow, and I was told I would catch men instead.
I walked on water until I looked at the waves and began to sink.
I denied my Lord three times before the cock crew, and I preached at Pentecost.
I held the coats of the men who stoned Stephen.
A light blinded me on a road, and a voice asked why I was persecuting him.
I wrote letters to the Romans and Corinthians, and I said I have fought a good fight.
I kept the bag, and I complained that costly ointment should have been sold.
I asked what they would give me, and they counted out thirty pieces of silver.
I betrayed my Master with a kiss in the garden of Gethsemane.
I once said let us also go, that we may die with him.
I said I would not believe unless I put my finger into the print of the nails.
I am the doubting disciple, and I cried out my Lord and my God.
I was one of seven chosen to serve tables, full of faith and the Holy Ghost.
I preached a long sermon on Israel's history, and my face shone like an angel's.
I was the first Christian martyr, stoned while I prayed for my killers.
My two sisters sent word that the one whom the Lord loved was sick.
Jesus wept before he came to my tomb.
I had been dead four days when I was called to come forth, still in grave clothes.
I was cumbered about with much serving and complained about my sister.
I was told that only one thing was needful, and that my sister had chosen it.
I said I believe you are the Christ, before my brother Lazarus was raised.
I was rich, but I was little of stature.
I climbed a sycamore tree just to see over the crowd.
I was a chief publican in Jericho, and I promised to restore fourfold.
I was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, and I came by night.
I asked how a man could be born when he is old.
I was told you must be born again, and I brought myrrh and aloes for the burial.
My wife sent me a warning about a dream she had suffered.
I asked what is truth, and I found no fault in the man before me.
I washed my hands before the multitude and delivered Jesus to be crucified.
My name means the son of consolation, and I sold my land for the apostles.
I vouched for a feared new convert when the disciples were afraid of him.
I traveled with Paul, then parted from him over whether to take Mark.
My mother was Eunice and my grandmother was Lois.
I was told to let no man despise my youth.
Paul called me his own son in the faith and wrote me two letters.
I was a tiller of the ground, and my offering was not accepted.
I asked whether I was my brother's keeper.
I killed Abel in a field and was marked and sent to wander.
I lived three hundred sixty-five years, which was short for my day.
I walked with God, and I was not, for God took me.
I never died, and my son was Methuselah.
I brought out bread and wine to a victorious warrior.
I was king of Salem and priest of the most high God.
Abraham paid me tithes, and Hebrews says I had no beginning of days.
I was hired to curse a nation, but I could only bless it.
An angel stood in my path with a drawn sword, and I did not see him.
My donkey spoke to me and asked what I had done to deserve three beatings.
